title: Console request acceptance gateway and evidence rubric for reporting & exports
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a structured acceptance gateway and evidence rubric for Console reporting and export requests (non-bug) to speed triage, enforce enterprise controls, and create deterministic prioritization for PM/Eng. This ticket defines the rubric, the intake form fields, automated gating rules for escalations, and the minimal deliverables for a request to move from Triage -> Planned. Goal: reduce ambiguous asks and accelerate delivery of high-impact exports for enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: A web-based intake form exists in the Console Request flow capturing required evidence for enterprise exports (see intake_form_fields)
An automated triage rule classifies requests into lanes: Self-serve, Engineering-backed scheduled export, One-off ad-hoc export, and Enterprise connector. Rules are documented and tested.
A prioritization calculator (spreadsheet + sample implementation) maps inputs to a recommended priority score and recommended SLA lane.
Documentation page outlining the rubric and SLA lanes is published and linked from the intake form.
Two pilot requests from enterprise customers processed end-to-end using the new gateway; outcomes logged in ticket comments and lessons captured.
intake_form_fields: Business objective and measurable outcome (why this export matters)
Expected consumer (BI, data engineering, support, legal)
Desired format and transport (CSV, Parquet, S3, BigQuery connector, webhook)
Retention window and sample size (days, rows)
Compliance or legal constraints (PII, GDPR, HIPAA) - yes/no and details
Example query or sample schema and a sample output CSV (attach)
Acceptable latency for initial job and for subsequent runs
Fallback if request is delayed or denied (business impact)
Requested completion date and priority justification
prioritization_rubric: Customer revenue signal: enterprise customers with > $50k ARR weighted heavily
Compliance requirement: any export tagged as compliance => auto-escalate to P0/P1
Reusability factor: features that generalize across multiple customers increase score
Engineering complexity estimate (S/M/L) reduces score proportionally
Operational cost impact: expected monthly compute/storage cost on Redwood; high cost reduces priority unless offset by business value
Time-sensitivity multiplier: regulatory deadlines or contract commitments increase priority
Product strategy alignment: cross-check against current roadmap initiatives (e.g., billing exports, tenant analytics)
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: building a generic connector (higher upfront cost) vs delivering ad-hoc CSVs for critical customers (fast but non-scalable). We'll favor scalable connectors for reuse unless customer commitment/revenue justifies bespoke work.
Tradeoff: strict intake gate increases time-to-first-response but reduces wasted engineering cycles. We'll implement a soft-gate (required fields) with PM review for edge cases during the pilot.
Risk: exposing large raw telemetry may increase security/compliance surface. Any request flagged as 'compliance' requires legal approval and will follow Private deployment guidance if sensitive.
We will not initially support real-time streaming connectors (Kafka/CDC) in phase 1; those are scoped to a follow-up initiative if demand is proven.
decisions: Decision 2026-03-05: Require a sample output file and a business outcome for any enterprise export before scheduling engineering work.
Decision 2026-03-07: Compliance-tagged requests auto-escalate to P0 and require legal sign-off; PM to route to Dedicated/Private teams as needed.
Decision 2026-03-10: Pilot the rubric with two customers (AcmeCorp, Nimbus Analytics); measure time-to-start and rework rate.
Decision 2026-03-12: Prioritization calculator will run as a simple spreadsheet initially and later be embedded in the intake flow as a read-only recommendation.
